다음 글의 표시된 ⓐ~ⓖ 중 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고른 것은?

Hajun applied to the soccer club because many of his classmates ⓐ[did], even though he preferred activities indoors. Only after he ⓑ[had become] a member did he realize that soccer did not suit him. Why do you think he made that choice? A wish to belong to a group can ⓒ[cause students choose] what their peers choose. The tendency to copy other people's behavior ⓓ[is called] the bandwagon effect. To make a choice of your own, first ask yourself ⓔ[what do you really want]. ⓕ[Despite your choice may differ] from your friends', you need not be afraid to act on it. Choosing what is right for you can leave you ⓖ[satisfied with your decision].
solution: ⓒ는 cause가 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취하므로 cause students to choose로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ는 ask yourself에 이어지는 간접의문문이므로 what you really want가 적절하다. ⓕ는 뒤에 절이 이어지므로 Despite를 Although로 바꿔야 한다. ⓐ의 did는 앞의 applied를 대신하며, ⓑ의 과거완료는 깨달음보다 앞선 가입을 나타내므로 옳다.

body:
다음 글의 표시된 ⓐ~ⓖ 중 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고른 것은?

Creating obstacles before attempting a task enables those who lack confidence ⓐ[make excuses] if they perform poorly. They may do this ⓑ[because of they place] greater value on the outcome than on the process. Although such excuses can keep a poor result ⓒ[from damaging] their self-esteem for a while, the habit may lead ⓓ[to failing repeatedly] at tasks they find difficult. ⓔ[Paying closer attention to the process] may reduce the pressure they feel and help them feel more encouraged to try. Even when disappointed with a result, they should not let themselves ⓕ[to feel] hopeless. For students facing such difficulties, the most important step ⓖ[is finding] their own way to handle negative feelings.
solution: ⓐ는 enable의 목적격 보어이므로 to make excuses로 고쳐야 하며, 목적어에 붙은 관계절 때문에 구조를 놓치지 않아야 한다. ⓑ는 뒤에 절이 이어지므로 because they place가 적절하다. ⓕ는 사역동사 let의 목적격 보어이므로 동사원형 feel로 고쳐야 한다. ⓓ의 to는 전치사이므로 동명사 failing이 올 수 있고, ⓔ와 ⓖ의 동명사구는 각각 주어와 보어로 적절하게 쓰였다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

The UNESCO King Sejong Literacy Prize recognizes efforts to help people learn to read and write. Its name honors King Sejong, whose achievements include the creation of Hangeul. Among the prize winners is Ageing Nepal. Its literacy program teaches older adults basic reading and writing in Nepali and English, helping them lead more independent lives in their communities. Another winner is a center at Concordia University in Canada. This center produced an interactive educational application and made it available without charge. The application has contributed to improving literacy in Africa.
choices: The prize recognizes achievements in developing new food crops.
Ageing Nepal teaches older adults only in English.
Ageing Nepal helps older adults become more independent through literacy education.
The center at Concordia University charges users for its application.
The Canadian center's application was developed to teach plant breeding.
solution: Ageing Nepal은 노인들에게 네팔어와 영어 읽기·쓰기를 가르쳐 지역 사회에서 더 독립적으로 생활하도록 돕는다. 따라서 문해 교육을 통해 노인들의 자립을 돕는다는 ③이 글의 내용과 일치한다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

After reaching Nigeria, Dr. Hahn discovered that cassava was the country's main food. Diseases caused by viruses and bacteria easily damaged the plant, resulting in poor harvests. He therefore aimed to produce cassava that could resist diseases and provide more food. Finding useful information was difficult, however. Since cassava was not a cash crop, researchers had paid little attention to studying or improving it. Dr. Hahn also lacked personal experience with the plant: he had neither seen nor tasted it before.
choices: Which plant was Nigeria's main food?
What caused damage to the cassava plants?
What improvements did Dr. Hahn want to make to cassava?
Why had cassava received little attention from researchers?
How many cassava plants did Dr. Hahn examine when he first arrived?
solution: 지문에는 나이지리아의 주식, 카사바를 손상시키는 원인, 품종 개량의 목표와 연구가 부족했던 이유가 제시되어 있다. 그러나 한 박사가 처음 도착했을 때 조사한 카사바의 수는 나오지 않으므로 ⑤에는 답할 수 없다.

body:
다음 글을 통해 추론할 수 있는 것은?

Dr. Hahn's field was plant breeding. Having experienced hunger while growing up after the Korean War, he hoped to help others facing the same difficulty. In 1971, he had opportunities to work at Cambridge University and at an agricultural research institute in Nigeria. He visited Nigeria while traveling to Cambridge for an interview. Nigeria was suffering from the effects of a civil war, and over half a million people faced starvation. Seeing their situation, he decided to help. After persuading his family, he moved to Nigeria.
choices: His own experience of hunger helped him understand the needs of people in Nigeria.
He first became interested in plant breeding after moving to Nigeria.
His visit to Nigeria took place after he completed his Cambridge interview.
He moved to Nigeria because the civil war had left everyone with enough food.
His family persuaded him to choose Nigeria before he visited the country.
solution: 한 박사는 성장기에 굶주림을 경험했고, 같은 어려움을 겪는 사람들을 돕고 싶어 했다. 이러한 경험과 나이지리아의 기아 상황을 연결하면 자신의 경험이 현지 사람들의 처지를 이해하는 데 도움이 되었음을 추론할 수 있다. ③과 ⑤는 지문에 제시된 사건의 순서나 설득의 주체를 바꾸었다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Dr. Hahn's agricultural work extended beyond cassava to crops such as yams, sweet potatoes, and bananas. Requests for assistance also came from other African nations. He visited those countries and explained to farmers and scholars how to cultivate the improved varieties. His work on developing new cassava varieties and spreading them across Africa lasted 23 years. He departed from Nigeria in 1994, but his efforts to fight hunger are still remembered. He believed that people should devote themselves to work that benefits humanity, and he said he would make the same choice if he could live his life again.
choices: His work involved improving several kinds of food crops.
People in other African countries requested his assistance.
He taught both farmers and scholars how to cultivate improved varieties.
He spent 23 years developing cassava varieties before beginning to distribute them.
He expressed a willingness to make the same choice again.
solution: 23년은 새로운 카사바 품종을 개발하고 아프리카에 보급하는 데 들인 기간 전체를 가리킨다. 개발에만 23년을 쓴 뒤 보급을 시작했다는 ④는 개발과 보급의 관계를 잘못 설명한 것이다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 있는 질문만을 <보기>에서 고른 것은?

Dr. Hahn learned that cassava had reached Africa through Europeans who had colonized Brazil. This discovery led him to Brazil to investigate the original plant. When he returned to Nigeria, he brought Brazilian cassava seeds with him. He also gathered local cassava varieties from different parts of Nigeria, but they did not show the disease resistance he was seeking. Later, he found a disease-resistant plant resembling cassava. By crossing that plant with Brazilian cassava, he eventually developed improved varieties. The work took five years, and the resulting varieties produced larger harvests than local cassava and survived diseases.

<보기>
ㄱ. Why did Dr. Hahn travel to Brazil?
ㄴ. What was the name of the disease-resistant plant that resembled cassava?
ㄷ. Which plants did Dr. Hahn cross to develop the improved varieties?
ㄹ. How many Nigerian cassava varieties did Dr. Hahn collect?
solution: 브라질 방문 목적은 원래의 카사바를 연구하는 것이므로 ㄱ에 답할 수 있다. 또한 내병성이 있는 유사 식물과 브라질 카사바를 교배했다고 했으므로 ㄷ에도 답할 수 있다. 유사 식물의 이름과 수집한 현지 품종의 정확한 수는 제시되지 않아 ㄴ과 ㄹ에는 답할 수 없다.

body:
다음 글에서 추론한 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?

Persuading Nigerian farmers to grow the improved cassava proved difficult because they were unwilling to accept advice from a foreigner. Dr. Hahn offered the varieties free of charge at places such as markets, churches, and schools. He also visited homes to explain their advantages. On some occasions, he put the new plants in farmers' fields without informing them. His colleagues feared this would anger the farmers, whereas he expected the plants to be welcomed as a gift from God. Farmers eventually recognized the advantages and increasingly grew the improved cassava. Hunger decreased, and selling cassava left over after meeting their needs brought farmers additional income. Nigeria later became the world's largest cassava producer.
choices: The farmers' early resistance shows that the improved varieties had already failed in their fields.
His colleagues' concerns establish that farmers became angry whenever they discovered the new plants.
The improved varieties helped address food shortages and also created opportunities for farmers to earn extra money.
The free distribution of plants means that farmers earned additional income from selling the plants back to Dr. Hahn.
Nigeria became the largest cassava producer before farmers began to recognize the advantages of the improved varieties.
solution: 새 품종 보급 이후 굶주리는 사람이 줄었고, 농민들은 필요한 양을 제외하고 남은 카사바를 팔아 추가 소득을 얻었다. 따라서 식량 부족 완화와 경제적 이익이라는 두 효과를 연결한 ③이 적절하다. ②는 동료들의 우려를 실제로 일어난 일로 바꾸었고, ⑤는 사건의 선후 관계를 뒤집었다.

body:
다음 글의 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 어법상 알맞게 짝지어진 것은?

Rockwell’s paintings (A)[shows / show] scenes of ordinary life as well as social issues. Looking closely at these paintings can help us (B)[understand / understanding] his ideas.
solution: 첫 문장의 주어는 복수 명사인 Rockwell’s paintings이므로 동사는 show가 알맞다. help는 목적격 보어로 동사원형이나 to부정사를 취할 수 있으므로, 제시된 두 형태 중에서는 understand를 써야 한다.

body: 다음 중 어법상 옳지 않은 문장은?
choices: The doctor pretends to check the doll’s heart.
The girl wants to get her doll examine by the doctor.
The doctor’s bag is beneath the chair.
The girl holds up her doll while facing the doctor.
The kindness of the doctor gives viewers a warm feeling.
solution: 인형은 진찰하는 주체가 아니라 진찰을 받는 대상이다. 따라서 get + 목적어 + 과거분사 구조를 사용하여 examine을 examined로 고쳐야 한다.

body:
다음 글의 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 어법상 알맞게 짝지어진 것은?

In The Connoisseur, Rockwell included an abstract painting. Let us (A)[consider / to consider] his choice of technique. He used the drip technique, (B)[that / which] modernist artists also used at the time.
solution: 사역동사 let의 목적격 보어 자리에는 동사원형 consider가 와야 한다. 쉼표 뒤에서 앞의 the drip technique을 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로는 that이 아니라 which를 쓴다.

body:
다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 어법상 알맞게 짝지어진 것은?

The Problem We All Live With presents a girl (A)[guarding / guarded] by people with armbands. The painting leads viewers to ask (B)[what / how] social issue Rockwell wished to show. Its background is Ruby Bridges’ walk to school, during which she passed a crowd (C)[protesting / was protesting] her enrollment.
solution: 소녀는 보호받는 대상이므로 (A)에는 수동의 의미를 나타내는 guarded가 알맞다. (B)에는 social issue를 수식하여 ‘어떤 사회 문제’를 뜻하는 what이 필요하다. (C)에는 a crowd를 뒤에서 수식하는 현재분사 protesting을 써야 하며, 관계사 없이 was protesting을 바로 연결할 수는 없다.

body: 다음 각 문장을 화살표 뒤의 문장으로 바꾸었을 때, 어법과 원문의 시제 관계를 모두 바르게 유지하지 못한 것은?
choices:
Digital artworks that are produced with computers can evoke emotions.
→ Digital artworks produced with computers can evoke emotions.

Works made with digital devices differ from those made by traditional methods.
→ Works made with digital devices differ from those that are made by traditional methods.

It is said that digital technology has broadened the range of artistic expression.
→ Digital technology is said to broaden the range of artistic expression.

There are various forms of art that use digital devices.
→ There are various forms of art using digital devices.

Some films are both produced and edited with digital technology.
→ Some films are produced as well as edited with digital technology.
solution: ③의 원문은 현재완료 has broadened를 사용하여 현재까지 이루어진 확장을 나타낸다. 이를 주어 + is said + to부정사 구조로 바꾸면서 시제 관계를 유지하려면 완료부정사 to have broadened를 써야 한다. 나머지는 관계절의 축약·복원이나 병렬 표현의 전환이 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 표시된 부분 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것만을 모두 고른 것은?

In The Connoisseur, a gentleman studies an abstract painting. The contrast between the gentleman’s realistic appearance and the abstract image ⓐ[reveals] Rockwell’s use of different styles. Critics ⓑ[fascinating by abstract art] had devalued his realistic approach. Rockwell responded by creating an abstract painting of his own. His use of the drip technique, ⓒ[which modernist artists also employed], connects this work with the art of the time. Since the gentleman is shown from behind, viewers cannot be certain ⓓ[what he approves of the painting]. Rockwell leaves them ⓔ[to interpret] the man’s reaction for themselves.
solution: ⓑ에서 비평가들은 추상 미술에 매료된 대상이므로 fascinating을 fascinated로 고쳐야 한다. ⓓ의 he approves of the painting은 필요한 성분을 모두 갖춘 절이며, 문맥상 찬성 여부를 나타내므로 what 대신 whether를 써야 한다. ⓐ는 주어의 핵심 명사 contrast에 일치하는 단수 동사이고, ⓒ의 which는 employed의 목적어 역할을 한다. ⓔ의 leave + 목적어 + to부정사는 그들이 직접 해석하도록 맡긴다는 의미로 적절하다.

body:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

여행자들은 현지 전통을 존중할 필요가 있다.

<보기>
respect / need / traditions / Travelers / to / local

<조건>
• 모든 단어를 한 번씩 사용할 것.
• Travelers로 시작하는 6단어 문장으로 쓸 것.
answer: Travelers need to respect local traditions.
solution: ‘~할 필요가 있다’는 need to 뒤에 동사원형을 써서 나타낸다. respect의 목적어로 local traditions를 배열한다.

body:
러이 끄라통 축제에 관한 다음 우리말을 <보기>의 단어를 배열하여 영작하시오.

그 축제는 보통 11월에 열린다.

<보기>
in / takes / November / The / usually / place / festival

<조건>
• 모든 단어를 한 번씩 사용할 것.
• The festival로 시작하는 7단어 문장으로 쓸 것.
answer: The festival usually takes place in November.
solution: ‘열리다’는 take place로 나타내며, 주어가 단수이므로 takes place를 쓴다. 빈도부사 usually는 일반동사 앞에 놓고, 월 앞에는 전치사 in을 쓴다.

body:
지파이의 크기를 설명하는 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 문장을 완성하시오.

지파이는 여러분의 얼굴만큼 클 수 있다.

Ji pai can ______________________________.

<보기>
as / your / be / big / face / as

<조건>
• <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것.
• as ~ as 동등 비교구문을 사용할 것.
• 빈칸에 들어갈 6단어만 쓸 것.
answer: be as big as your face
solution: 동등 비교는 as와 as 사이에 형용사의 원급을 넣어 나타낸다. 조동사 can 뒤에는 동사원형 be를 쓰므로 be as big as your face가 된다.

body:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 배열하시오.

여행자들은 현지인들이 따르는 관습을 존중해야 한다.

<보기>
follow / should / the / local / respect / customs / Travelers / people

<조건>
• 모든 단어를 한 번씩 사용할 것.
• 목적격 관계대명사를 생략한 관계절로 customs를 수식할 것.
• Travelers로 시작하는 8단어 문장으로 쓸 것.
answer: Travelers should respect the customs local people follow.
solution: ‘현지인들이 따르는 관습’은 the customs that local people follow로 표현할 수 있다. 관계대명사 that은 follow의 목적어이므로 생략할 수 있으며, 이 관계절을 customs 뒤에 놓는다.

body:
스린 야시장의 분위기를 설명하는 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.

많은 사람들이 시장을 방문하면서, 분위기는 활기를 띠게 된다.

<보기>
visit / many people / the market / With / the atmosphere / becomes lively

<조건>
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것.
• visit만 알맞게 변형하고, 다른 단어는 추가하지 말 것.
• ‘with + 명사 + 현재분사’ 구문을 사용할 것.
• With로 시작하고, 부대상황을 나타내는 구 뒤에 쉼표를 쓸 것.
answer: With many people visiting the market, the atmosphere becomes lively.
solution: many people이 시장을 방문하는 능동 관계이므로 visit을 현재분사 visiting으로 바꾼다. With many people visiting the market 뒤에 주절 the atmosphere becomes lively를 연결한다.

body:
스린 야시장의 음식에 관한 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.

관광객들이 맛볼 수 있는 음식에는 신선한 굴로 채워진 오믈렛이 포함된다.

<보기>
fill / tourists / an omelet / can / The food / fresh oysters / includes / with / try

<조건>
• <보기>의 단어 및 표현을 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것.
• fill만 알맞게 변형하고, 다른 단어는 추가하지 말 것.
• food 뒤에는 목적격 관계대명사를 생략한 관계절을 쓸 것.
• omelet 뒤에는 과거분사로 시작하는 수식어구를 쓸 것.
• The food로 시작하는 12단어 문장으로 쓸 것.
answer: The food tourists can try includes an omelet filled with fresh oysters.
solution: The food 뒤에 목적격 관계대명사를 생략한 tourists can try를 연결하며, 문장의 본동사는 includes이다. 오믈렛은 굴로 채워지는 대상이므로 fill을 filled로 바꾸어 filled with fresh oysters로 수식한다. 주어의 중심어가 단수인 food라는 점에 유의한다.

body:
지속 가능한 여행에 관한 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.

현지 관습을 존중함으로써, 여행자들은 관광의 영향을 받는 공동체들을 보존하는 데 도움을 줄 수 있다.

<보기>
respect / travelers / by / communities / can / local customs / affect / tourism / By / help / preserve

<조건>

Have you ever heard of the "Eiffel Tower Effect?" When the Eiffel Tower was first built, the iron tower was very different from all the other architecture in Paris, which was mainly made of stone. Many local people disliked the tower and complained that it would ruin the beauty of Paris. Nevertheless, as the locals became familiar with the tower due to exposure, they became more and more fond of it, referring to it as the Tower of Love. This effect, also called the "Mere Exposure Effect," is found with people, too. Psychologist Robert Zajonc and his colleagues showed university students pictures of several faces. Some pictures were shown 25 times while others were shown only once or twice. Then, the students were shown a picture and asked to express how much they liked that person. The students liked the people they had seen more often better than those they had seen less frequently. This shows that the more we are exposed to something, the more favorably we view it.

Repeated exposure gradually changed the locals' negative attitude toward the tower.
Robert Zajonc carried out the experiment with his colleagues.

The experiment suggests that frequent exposure leads people to view something more positively.

When people do not have the confidence to perform tasks well, they are likely to create obstacles to success. This type of behavior is referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping enables people to make excuses for their poor performances. These excuses prevent the poor result from lowering their self-esteem. This might work in the short term. However, be careful! It could lead to repeated failures in certain tasks that you are not confident in doing.
If you are self-handicapping, it might be because you consider the results more important than the process. Focusing more on the process than the outcome may ease the pressure to perform well. Accordingly, you may feel more encouraged to try to do the challenging tasks. This can eventually stop your self-handicapping.

<보기>
(a) Self-handicapping can keep people's self-esteem from being lowered by poor results.
(b) Self-handicapping is helpful in the long run because it removes obstacles to success.
(c) People who self-handicap may value outcomes more than the process.
(d) Focusing on the result rather than the process can reduce the pressure to perform well.
(e) Feeling less pressure may make people more willing to attempt challenging tasks.

The girl suggests placing the title with a car image in the center.
Mike suggests putting a spacecraft at the bottom of the background.
solution: 대화에서 우주선(spacecraft)은 소녀가 배경의 위쪽(top)에 넣자고 제안했고, 마이크는 배경 아래쪽(bottom)에 지구 이미지를 넣고 싶어 했다. 따라서 '마이크가 배경 아래쪽에 우주선을 넣자고 제안했다'는 ⑤는 대화 내용과 일치하지 않는다. ①~④는 대화에 그대로 드러난다.

body:
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Another everyday item developed from space technology is the air purifier. A reliable source of food was vital for survival in space, so astronauts had to cultivate crops in the spacecraft. However, there was a major obstacle: when plants grow, ethylene gas is produced, which accelerates the aging of plants and the decaying of fruits. Since it was impossible to exchange gas for clean air while in space, scientists developed an air purification system to remove the gas. Although the goal was to eliminate ethylene, the system could get rid of other unwanted things from the air, too. A private company recognized the potential of the system and obtained a license to develop and commercialize it.
choices: Astronauts had to grow crops inside the spacecraft to secure a reliable source of fresh food.
Ethylene gas, produced as plants grow, speeds up the aging of plants and the decaying of fruits.
Because gas could not be exchanged for clean air in space, scientists created an air purification system.
Though designed to eliminate ethylene, the system could also remove other unwanted things from the air.
A private company built the air purification system from scratch and then sold its license to NASA.
solution: 본문에서는 한 민간 기업이 이미 개발된 공기 정화 시스템의 잠재력을 '알아보고(recognized)' 그것을 개발·상용화할 수 있는 '라이선스를 획득했다(obtained a license)'고 했다. 따라서 기업이 시스템을 처음부터 직접 만들어 NASA에 라이선스를 팔았다는 ⑤는 주체와 방향이 뒤바뀐 서술로 일치하지 않는다. ①~④는 모두 본문과 부합한다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

Coral reefs are crucial ecosystems that protect both marine life and people living near the sea. Coral reefs provide shelter to an abundance of marine life, such as fish and underwater plants. Because of the diversity of life found in coral reefs, they are often called "the rainforests of the sea." Nearly one quarter of all known marine species depend on coral reefs for survival — they hide themselves from predators, find food, reproduce, and raise their young in coral reefs.
choices: Coral reefs protect marine life but not people living near the sea.
Coral reefs are called "the rainforests of the sea" because of their bright colors.
About half of all known marine species depend on coral reefs for survival.
Some marine species raise their young in coral reefs.
Coral reefs provide shelter only to fish.
solution: 마지막 문장에 해양 생물들이 산호초에서 포식자를 피해 숨고, 먹이를 찾고, 번식하고, 새끼를 기른다(raise their young)고 나와 있으므로 ④가 글의 내용과 맞는다. ①은 산호초가 바닷가 근처에 사는 사람들도 보호한다는 내용과 어긋나고, ②는 별명의 이유가 색깔이 아니라 생물의 다양성(diversity of life)이다. ③은 절반이 아니라 약 4분의 1(one quarter)이며, ⑤는 물고기뿐 아니라 수중 식물에게도 서식처를 준다는 내용과 맞지 않는다.

body:
윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

A lot of people may be unfamiliar with the fact that there are forests in the sea, but the sea has forests, too. Sea forests are formed by marine plants, and numerous marine animals live there with them. That is, sea forests are habitats for underwater creatures and the leading contributors to creating a healthy marine ecosystem. However, uncontrolled human actions and climate change have threatened marine plants and the other creatures that live on them. So the Korean government designated May 10th every year as "Marine Gardening Day," the first in the world. It is meant to raise awareness of the seriousness of ocean pollution and the importance of creating sea forests. Accordingly, many organizations contribute to protecting and reinforcing the ecosystem in damaged ocean areas by planting marine plants. On a smaller scale, groups of people pick up trash along the coast on this day.
choices: What are sea forests formed by?
What has threatened marine plants and other sea creatures?
Which country was the first to designate Marine Gardening Day?
How many organizations plant marine plants on Marine Gardening Day?
What do groups of people do along the coast on Marine Gardening Day?
solution: 글에는 'many organizations'가 해양 식물을 심는다고만 나와 있고, 단체가 몇 개인지는 나오지 않으므로 ④에는 답할 수 없다. ①은 해양 식물(marine plants), ②는 무분별한 인간 활동과 기후 변화, ③은 한국(the Korean government, the first in the world), ⑤는 해안을 따라 쓰레기 줍기로 각각 답할 수 있다.

body:
윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것을 <보기>에서 모두 고른 것은?

In recent years, advanced technologies have been put in place to save coral reefs by monitoring, protecting, and restoring them in quick and efficient ways. Researchers from Florida introduced a soft jellyfish-like robot to monitor coral reefs without damaging their delicate bodies. In addition, an Australian research team invented an intelligent underwater robot to protect coral reefs from a dangerous species of starfish. The robot uses a camera and computerized vision system to scan the reefs and identify this starfish. When it encounters one, the robot uses a foldable arm to inject some toxic salt into the starfish and eliminate it. Meanwhile, 3D printing systems have been proposed in Hong Kong as one way to restore coral reef structures. The 3D printer creates artificial support for corals. An example is a block made of mud that lies on the floor of the ocean. It is shaped in a way that allows corals to attach to it and grow easily.

<보기>
a. The jellyfish-like robot was introduced to observe coral reefs without harming them.
b. The Australian robot was designed to protect a dangerous species of starfish from coral reefs.
c. The Australian robot recognizes the starfish by using a camera and a computerized vision system.
d. Researchers from Florida have already used 3D printing systems to restore coral reef structures.
e. The block created by the 3D printer is made of mud and helps corals attach to it and grow.
solution: a는 플로리다 연구진이 산호초의 연약한 몸체를 손상하지 않고 관찰하려고 해파리 모양 로봇을 도입했다는 내용과 맞는다. c는 카메라와 컴퓨터 시각 시스템으로 불가사리를 식별한다는 내용과 맞고, e는 진흙으로 만든 블록에 산호가 쉽게 붙어 자랄 수 있다는 내용과 맞는다. b는 보호 대상이 거꾸로 되어 있다(불가사리로부터 산호초를 보호함). d는 3D 프린팅 시스템이 플로리다가 아니라 홍콩에서, 그것도 이미 사용된 것이 아니라 제안된(proposed) 것이므로 틀렸다. 따라서 정답은 a, c, e이다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Now, look at The Connoisseur, created in 1962. In the painting, an abstract art piece is hung on the wall and a gentleman is looking at it. The man is painted realistically in Rockwell's typical style, but the abstract art piece shows splashes of paint in a variety of colors. After World War II, art critics fascinated by abstract art devalued Rockwell's realistic style. In response, Rockwell decided to paint his own abstract painting. He used the drip technique, which was used by modernist artists at that time. By combining these different styles in one art piece, Rockwell highlighted his identity as a painter as well as an illustrator. In addition, we can see the man only from the rear. Rockwell left the interpretation of the gentleman's reaction to us.
choices: The Connoisseur was created in 1962 and shows a gentleman looking at an abstract painting on the wall.
The abstract art piece is depicted with splashes of paint in various colors.
We are shown the gentleman's face clearly from the front of the painting.
Rockwell used the drip technique, which modernist artists used at that time.
Rockwell left it up to viewers to interpret the gentleman's reaction.
solution: 본문은 'we can see the man only from the rear'라고 하여 신사를 뒤에서만 볼 수 있다고 했다. 따라서 얼굴을 정면에서 뚜렷이 볼 수 있다는 ③은 글과 일치하지 않는다. 나머지 선지는 제작 연도, 추상화 묘사, 드립 기법, 해석을 관람객에게 맡긴 점 등 본문과 모두 일치한다.

body:
다음 대화의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

B: Jenny, do you happen to know Marc Chagall?
G: Of course. He is one of the most famous artists in the world.
B: I watched a TV program last week that introduced him and his paintings.
G: What was your impression of the paintings?
B: The colors were so beautiful and vivid that I couldn't take my eyes off them.
G: You know what? He is also famous for his book illustrations and stained glass art.
B: Really? I'm curious what they look like.
G: I have a photo book of his art. If you want, I can lend it to you.
B: Thank you.
choices: The boy got to know Chagall's paintings through a newspaper article.
Chagall is famous only for his oil paintings.
The boy was not impressed by the colors in Chagall's paintings.
The girl offers to lend the boy her photo book of Chagall's art.
The girl has never heard of Marc Chagall before.
solution: 대화 마지막에서 소녀는 'I have a photo book of his art. If you want, I can lend it to you.'라고 하며 책을 빌려주겠다고 제안하므로 ④가 일치한다. 소년은 TV 프로그램으로 그림을 알게 되었고(①×), 샤갈은 책 삽화와 스테인드글라스로도 유명하며(②×), 소년은 색채에 깊은 인상을 받았고(③×), 소녀는 샤갈을 이미 잘 알고 있다(⑤×).

다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

In a broad sense, digital art refers to any type of art that is created and displayed with the aid of digital devices. This artistic format emerged with the evolutionary progress in digital media and computers a few decades ago. There are many types of art that use digital technology. For instance, music can be recorded and then changed with the aid of digital devices, or music can be made only with computer software. Some movies are both created and edited digitally. Additionally, art museums offer exhibitions displaying famous paintings of the world on big digital screens.
choices: What does digital art refer to in a broad sense?
When did this artistic format emerge?
How can music be involved in digital art?
What do art museums display on big digital screens?
Who created the very first digital artwork in history?
solution: 본문에는 디지털 아트의 정의, 등장 시기(a few decades ago), 음악·영화·미술관 전시 등 구체적 예시가 제시되어 ①~④는 모두 답할 수 있다. 그러나 최초의 디지털 아트 작품을 누가 만들었는지는 언급되지 않으므로 ⑤는 답할 수 없다.

Many of Rockwell's works about everyday life are quite tender. An example is Doctor and the Doll, produced in 1929. The little girl, who seems to be about four or five years old, is facing the old man while holding up a doll. The man is wearing a black suit, and there is a doctor's bag under the chair. The girl has already put the doll's dress under her arm because she wants to get her doll examined by the doctor. The doctor is going along with her wish and is pretending to listen to the doll's heart. He is treating her and her doll carefully. This work helps us appreciate the innocence of children. The girl's cuteness and the doctor's kindness evoke a feeling of warmth, bringing tender smiles to viewers' faces.
choices: Doctor and the Doll, produced in 1929, is one of Rockwell's tender works about everyday life.
The little girl appears to be about four or five years old and is holding up a doll.
There is a doctor's bag placed under the chair, and the man is dressed in a black suit.
The doctor refuses the girl's wish and ignores her by turning away from the doll.
The girl's cuteness and the doctor's kindness create a warm feeling for viewers.
solution: 본문은 의사가 'going along with her wish'하며 인형의 심장 소리를 듣는 척하고 소녀와 인형을 조심스럽게 대한다고 했다. 따라서 소녀의 바람을 거절하고 외면한다는 ④는 글과 반대이다. 제작 연도, 소녀의 나이와 인형, 의사 가방과 검은 양복, 따뜻한 분위기는 모두 본문과 일치한다.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

This was painted in 1964. Along the street walks a little African American girl wearing a pure white dress and guarded by people wearing armbands. A tomato, perhaps thrown at her, is smashed on the ground while juice stains the wall above. The redness of the tomato easily captures the viewers' attention. The title of this work is The Problem We All Live With. It describes segregation and racism in the U.S. This work was inspired by Ruby Bridges' historic walk. Ruby was the first African American child to enter an elementary school for white children in New Orleans. On her first day of school, she walked past an angry crowd protesting her enrollment. The historical background made this painting an important symbol of the Civil Rights Movement in the U.S.
choices: The painting was created in 1964 and depicts an African American girl in a pure white dress.
The people wearing armbands threw tomatoes at the girl to protest her enrollment.
The redness of the smashed tomato easily draws the viewers' attention.
Ruby Bridges was the first African American child to enter a white children's elementary school in New Orleans.
The painting became an important symbol of the Civil Rights Movement in the U.S.
solution: 본문에서 완장을 찬 사람들은 소녀를 '보호하는(guarded)' 역할이며, 토마토는 (아마도) 성난 군중이 던진 것이다. 따라서 완장을 찬 사람들이 토마토를 던졌다는 ②는 글과 일치하지 않는다. 제작 연도와 흰 드레스, 토마토의 붉은색, 루비 브리지스에 관한 설명, 민권 운동의 상징이 된 점은 모두 본문과 일치한다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

Do you know what a jumpsuit is? It is usually a single item that covers your whole body, even your arms and legs. It is easy and quick to put on and to take off. As the name indicates, the jumpsuit began as clothing for jumping from planes. Later, designers transformed this functional design into luxurious women's fashion items seen in fashion shows around the world.
choices: 점프슈트는 보통 상의와 하의 두 벌로 이루어져 있다.
점프슈트는 입고 벗는 데 시간이 오래 걸린다.
점프슈트는 처음에 비행기에서 뛰어내릴 때 입는 옷이었다.
점프슈트는 오늘날 남성용 패션 아이템으로만 쓰인다.
solution: 'the jumpsuit began as clothing for jumping from planes'라고 했으므로 ④가 글의 내용과 일치합니다. 점프슈트는 'a single item'이고 팔과 다리까지 덮으며(①·②), 입고 벗기가 쉽고 빠릅니다(③). 오늘날에는 고급 여성 패션 아이템이 되었다고 했으므로 ⑤도 틀립니다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

You have probably owned a pair of sneakers for everyday activities or sports. They are a type of athletic shoe designed specifically to be worn for physical activities and sports. So, why are they called sneakers? The name "sneakers" is derived from the term "to sneak up." Due to the fact that sneakers' soles are mostly made of rubber, they make little noise when people walk. Before rubber, leather was used for the sole of shoes. Traditional leather shoes make a lot of noise, and it is easier to hear the person wearing them.
choices: 스니커즈는 신체 활동과 운동을 위해 고안된 운동화이다.
고무가 쓰이기 전에는 신발 밑창에 가죽이 사용되었다.
전통적인 가죽 신발은 걸을 때 소리가 많이 난다.
solution: 'sneakers' soles are mostly made of rubber'라고 했으므로 스니커즈 밑창은 대부분 가죽이 아니라 고무로 만들어집니다. 따라서 ③이 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다. 가죽은 고무가 쓰이기 전의 밑창 재료였습니다.

body:
다음 대화를 읽고 답할 수 있는 질문은?

G: James, have you finished the career path survey?
B: Yes. I'm interested in working in the field of fashion. I want to be a fashion stylist.
G: I believe you will make a good fashion stylist. I always feel that you know how to dress well.

G: As you know, I'm interested in cars. I want to become a car designer.
B: A car designer? What exactly does a car designer do?
G: A car designer tries to improve the style and comfort of a vehicle.
B: That's cool. I want to ride in a car you've designed someday.
choices: What does James want to be in the future?
Where does Chloe want to work after graduation?
When did James finish the career path survey?
What kind of car does Chloe like best?
Why did James become interested in fashion?
solution: James가 'I want to be a fashion stylist.'라고 말했으므로 ①에는 답할 수 있습니다. Chloe가 일하고 싶은 장소, 설문을 끝낸 시점, Chloe가 가장 좋아하는 차종, James가 패션에 관심을 갖게 된 이유는 대화에 나오지 않습니다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

Whether they are loose fit or slim fit, most of you have at least one pair of blue jeans. They were named "jeans" because they were made of jean, a sort of tough cotton cloth. The word jean is a modification of Gênes, the French name of the Italian city of Genoa. In the 17th and 18th centuries, Genoa was a major center for trade. Sailing merchants from Genoa traded their goods throughout Europe, particularly in England and France. One of the items that made Genoa famous was a strong cotton cloth, ideally suited to making tough work clothes. The cloth was most likely colored blue. French was widely spoken in Europe at that time, so the cloth was called "bleu de Gênes" (the blue of Genoa). This is how the pants made with "bleu de Gênes" became known as blue jeans in English.
choices: Jeans got their name from a French merchant who sold them.
The word jean comes from the Italian name for the city of Genoa.
Sailing merchants from Genoa traded their goods only within Italy.
At that time, English was the most widely spoken language in Europe.
The strong cotton cloth from Genoa was well suited to making tough work clothes.
solution: 'a strong cotton cloth, ideally suited to making tough work clothes'라고 했으므로 ⑤가 일치합니다. jeans라는 이름은 옷감 jean에서 왔고(①), jean은 Genoa의 프랑스어 이름 Gênes가 바뀐 말입니다(②). 상인들은 유럽 전역, 특히 영국과 프랑스에서 교역했고(③), 당시 유럽에서 널리 쓰인 언어는 프랑스어였습니다(④).

body:
다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

People wear tuxedos when a formal dress code is required, like for the opera, dinner parties, or awards shows. The tuxedo likely got its name from Tuxedo Park, one of the first gated communities in New York. In the late 19th century, men usually wore jackets with long tails that reached their knees on formal occasions. One evening, a man showed up with a short black jacket without tails in Tuxedo Park. The male guests who stayed there were fascinated by the new jacket and started to wear the same style. Later, more people asked their tailors to make them a jacket "like the one worn in Tuxedo Park." At first, this style of jacket was considered less formal than one with long tails. As more and more men wore the shorter style, it eventually replaced the longer version.
choices: Where did the tuxedo likely get its name?
Who was the man who first wore the short black jacket in Tuxedo Park?
What kind of jackets did men usually wear on formal occasions in the late 19th century?
How did the male guests in Tuxedo Park react to the new jacket?
What happened as more and more men wore the shorter style?
solution: 글에는 'a man'이 짧은 검은 재킷을 입고 나타났다고만 나오고, 그 사람이 누구인지는 나오지 않으므로 ②에는 답할 수 없습니다. ①은 Tuxedo Park, ③은 무릎까지 오는 긴 꼬리가 달린 재킷, ④는 매료되어 같은 스타일을 입기 시작했다는 것, ⑤는 짧은 스타일이 결국 긴 스타일을 대체했다는 것으로 답할 수 있습니다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

On beaches and at pools, everyone seems to wear simple shoes with a band across the top of the foot and between the big toe and second toe. Amazingly, they are one of the oldest shoes in history. Ancient Egyptian paintings show they were worn around 4,000 B.C. Due to the fact that they have such a long history, they have different names all around the world. The Japanese call them zories. New Zealanders call them jandals, which is a shortened form of "Japanese sandals." However, in the USA, these shoes are called "flip-flops." Just walk around in a pair of them, and you can easily guess why they got this name. The rubber soles hit the bottom of your feet as you walk, making a flip-flop, flip-flop sound. The sound became the name of the shoes, flip-flops.
choices: The shoes have a band that goes between the big toe and second toe.
People wore these shoes as early as around 4,000 B.C.
The name "jandals" came from the sound the shoes make when people walk.
In Japan, people call these shoes zories.
In the USA, the shoes were named after the sound their rubber soles make.
solution: 'jandals'는 'Japanese sandals'를 줄인 말이라고 했으므로, 걷는 소리에서 나온 이름이라는 ③은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다. 소리에서 나온 이름은 미국에서 쓰는 'flip-flops'입니다(⑤). ①, ②, ④는 모두 글에 나온 내용입니다.

body:
다음 영어 단어의 우리말 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?

confidence
solution: confidence는 '자신감'이라는 뜻의 명사이다. 지문의 'do not have the confidence to perform tasks well(과제를 잘 해낼 자신감이 없다)'에서 그 쓰임을 확인할 수 있다. 따라서 정답은 ①이다.

body:
다음 우리말 뜻에 해당하는 영어 단어로 알맞은 것은?

장애물
solution: '장애물'에 해당하는 단어는 obstacle이다. 지문의 'create obstacles to success(성공에 장애물을 만들다)'에서 쓰였다. process(과정), outcome(결과), excuse(변명), pressure(압박)는 뜻이 다르므로 정답은 ②이다.

body:
다음 우리말 뜻에 해당하는 영어 표현으로 알맞은 것은?

자존감
solution: '자존감'은 self-esteem이다. 지문의 'lowering their self-esteem(그들의 자존감을 낮추는 것)'에서 확인할 수 있다. self-handicapping은 '자기 불구화', short term은 '단기', poor performance는 '좋지 못한 수행'을 뜻하므로 정답은 ①이다.

body:
밑줄 친 단어와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

Focusing more on the process may ease the pressure to perform well.
solution: ease는 '(고통·부담 등을) 덜어 주다, 완화하다'라는 뜻으로 relieve와 의미가 가장 가깝다. 지문에서 과정에 집중하는 것이 수행 압박을 '덜어 준다'는 맥락으로 쓰였다. increase(늘리다)는 반대 의미이므로 정답은 ②이다.

body:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?

These excuses _______ the poor result from lowering their self-esteem.
solution: 'prevent A from -ing'는 'A가 ~하는 것을 막다'라는 뜻의 구문이다. 빈칸 뒤에 'from lowering'이 이어지므로 이 구문을 완성하는 prevent가 알맞다. 변명들이 좋지 못한 결과가 자존감을 낮추는 것을 '막는다'는 의미이므로 정답은 ①이다.

body:
밑줄 친 단어의 반의어(antonym)로 알맞은 것은?

You may feel more encouraged to try to do the challenging tasks.
solution: challenging은 '도전적인, 어려운'이라는 뜻이므로 반의어는 '쉬운'을 뜻하는 easy이다. difficult, hard, tough, demanding은 모두 challenging과 비슷한 '어려운'이라는 의미이다. 따라서 정답은 ③이다.

body: 다음 중 영어 단어와 우리말 뜻의 연결이 바르지 않은 것은?
solution: excuse는 '변명'이라는 뜻이며 '자존감'은 self-esteem이다. 따라서 'excuse – 자존감'의 연결이 바르지 않다. 나머지 ①, ②, ③, ⑤는 모두 올바른 연결이므로 정답은 ④이다.

body:
빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말이 바르게 짝지어진 것은?

If you consider the results more important than the process, you may (A)_______ obstacles to success. However, focusing more on the process may (B)_______ the pressure to perform well.
solution: (A) 결과를 과정보다 중시하면 성공에 장애물을 '만든다(create)'는 흐름이 자연스럽다. (B) 과정에 집중하면 수행 압박을 '덜어 준다(ease)'는 의미가 알맞다. remove(제거하다), increase(늘리다)는 문맥과 맞지 않으므로 정답은 ②이다.

choices: The importance of healthy eating habits

body:

Loi Krathong is a famous festival of lights in Thailand. During the festival, people release floating lanterns called krathongs into the water while making wishes. In Sukhothai, visitors can also enjoy fireworks, folk dances, and beautiful light shows.
choices: A Festival of Lights and Wishes
How to Prepare Traditional Thai Food
The Most Dangerous Activities in Thailand
Shopping at Night Markets in Asia
The History of Water Sports in Thailand
solution: 제목을 고를 때는 글 전체에서 중심이 되는 소재를 찾아야 합니다. 이 글은 태국의 러이끄라통 축제에서 소원을 빌며 등불을 띄우고 여러 공연을 즐기는 모습을 소개합니다. 축제의 특징인 빛과 소원을 모두 담은 ①이 가장 적절합니다.

choices: Canyoning should be avoided because it is always dangerous.
Dalat is mainly known for its traditional food.
Waterfalls are suitable only for sightseeing.
Artificial water parks are more exciting than natural places.
Datanla Waterfall is a great place to experience exciting canyoning activities.
solution: 글쓴이는 신나는 야외 활동을 좋아하는 사람들에게 다딴라 폭포의 캐니어닝을 추천하고 있습니다. 집라인, 자연 물 미끄럼틀, 폭포 하강은 그곳에서 경험할 수 있는 활동의 예시입니다. 따라서 다딴라 폭포가 짜릿한 캐니어닝을 즐기기 좋은 곳이라는 ⑤가 정답입니다.

Are you planning to visit Shilin Night Market? Arrive at around 7 to 8 p.m., when everything is set up and the market becomes lively. Start with ji pai if you enjoy crispy fried chicken. You can also try oyster omelet with sweet sauce. After walking around the market, refresh yourself with some sweet papaya milk juice. These foods will make your visit even more enjoyable.
choices: To explain why tourists should avoid visiting night markets
To introduce the best time to visit Shilin Night Market and recommend foods to try
To compare the nutritional value of three Taiwanese dishes
To describe how street food prices have changed over the years
To encourage local residents to open new restaurants
solution: 글쓴이가 독자에게 어떤 정보를 전달하려는지 살펴보면 됩니다. 이 글은 스린 야시장을 방문하기 좋은 시간인 오후 7~8시를 안내하고, 지파이와 굴 오믈렛 등 추천 음식도 소개합니다. 음식의 영양이나 가격 변화를 분석하는 글이 아니므로 방문 시간과 추천 음식을 안내하는 ②가 정답입니다.

body:

Sukhothai is a special place to experience Loi Krathong because it is the birthplace of the festival. Its celebration lasts for about five days and is the biggest in Thailand. Visitors can release floating lanterns, enjoy fireworks, and watch light and sound shows. Since the festival date changes every year, visitors should check the date before traveling.
choices: Why Thai Festivals Have Different Dates Every Year
The Development of Modern Entertainment in Thailand
Traditional Music and Dance around the World
Experience the Special Charm of Loi Krathong in Sukhothai
A Guide to Thailand's Famous Night Markets

body:
다음 글을 요약한 문장의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Sustainable travelers should think about more than their own enjoyment. They can reduce plastic waste and avoid disturbing wild animals. They should also respect the customs of local communities. In addition, choosing local tour guides and guest houses can help local businesses.

Sustainable travel requires travelers to (A)________ the natural environment and local cultures while (B)________ local businesses.
solution: 요약문을 완성하려면 본문에 제시된 지속 가능한 여행의 실천 방법을 연결해야 합니다. 자연환경과 지역 문화를 보호한다는 의미이므로 (A)에는 protect가 적절합니다. 지역 사업체를 지원한다는 내용에는 supporting이 알맞으며, while 뒤에서도 자연스럽게 연결됩니다. 따라서 정답은 ③입니다.

body:
다음 글의 주제로 가장 알맞은 것은?

Tourism can bring enjoyment to travelers, but it can also affect the places they visit. Sustainable travel aims to maintain tourism without harming natural or cultural environments. To practice it, travelers should reduce pollution, save water, and avoid disturbing wildlife. They also need to respect local traditions and support local communities. Spending money on local services, such as tour guides and guest houses, can help the local economy. These actions show that responsible travel requires attention to several connected aspects rather than just one.
choices: The role of local businesses in attracting more tourists
The importance of protecting wildlife instead of promoting tourism
The reasons travelers prefer traditional accommodations
The difficulties of maintaining tourism without modern technology
The need to balance environmental, social, and economic responsibilities in sustainable travel
solution: 이 문항에서는 여러 세부 내용을 하나의 주제로 통합하는 것이 중요합니다. 글은 환경 보호뿐 아니라 지역 사회 존중과 지역 경제 지원까지 함께 고려해야 한다고 설명합니다. ①과 ②는 각각 경제와 환경이라는 한 측면에만 초점을 맞춘 선택지입니다. 세 가지 측면을 모두 반영한 ⑤가 정답입니다.

Some travelers may think that canyoning is simply another way to enjoy the beautiful scenery of Dalat. However, canyoning at Datanla Waterfall offers much more than a view. Travelers can fly down a cable while watching the waterfall, slide into cool water along a natural rock surface, and walk down a vertical waterfall with the help of a rope. Each activity allows visitors to experience nature in an exciting and active way. For adventure seekers, these experiences make Datanla Waterfall a place worth visiting.
choices: Datanla Waterfall offers adventure seekers thrilling ways to experience nature.
Canyoning is mainly an activity for studying the geological features of waterfalls.
Watching waterfalls from a distance is more enjoyable than participating in outdoor activities.
Dalat should replace its natural attractions with artificial water parks.
Travelers should choose peaceful sightseeing instead of challenging outdoor sports.
solution: 첫 문장만 읽으면 단순한 자연경관 소개로 생각하기 쉽지만, However 뒤에서 글의 핵심이 드러납니다. 글쓴이는 캐니어닝을 통해 자연을 짜릿하고 역동적으로 경험할 수 있다는 점을 강조합니다. 집라인, 자연 물 미끄럼틀, 폭포 하강은 이를 뒷받침하는 사례이므로 ①이 정답입니다.

Loi Krathong is celebrated throughout Thailand, but Sukhothai has a special connection to the festival because it is its birthplace. During the celebration, people release floating lanterns while making wishes. Visitors can also enjoy fireworks, folk dances, and light and sound shows. The festival usually takes place in November, but its exact date changes from year to year because it follows the Thai lunar calendar. Therefore, travelers should confirm the date before planning their visit.

Sukhothai is an (A)________ destination for experiencing Loi Krathong because of its historical connection and various attractions, but visitors need to (B)________ the festival date before traveling.
solution: 요약문의 앞부분과 뒷부분에 각각 대응하는 내용을 찾아야 합니다. 수코타이는 축제의 발상지이면서 다양한 행사를 즐길 수 있는 곳이므로 (A)에는 '이상적인'이라는 뜻의 ideal이 적절합니다. 축제 날짜는 해마다 달라 방문 전에 확인해야 하므로 (B)에는 check가 들어갑니다. 두 조건을 모두 충족하는 정답은 ②입니다.
